about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: Artesian Wastewater Management, Inc.
channels.legal_basis: 7 Del. C. 6028(a): a person causing an environmental release (sewage of 10,000 gallons or more, 6002(20)) "shall report such an incident to the Department as soon as the person has knowledge"; DNREC posts it on its website "no later than 1 business day after the release is reported"; permitted discharges are exempt
channels.note: Artesian Wastewater Management, Inc.'s sewage releases reach the public through DNREC's Recent Releases list when reported under 6028 (sewage from 10,000 gallons; smaller ones when reported), read by this site. The operator's own pages were not searched individually.

channels.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
channels.name: Delaware DNREC (beach advisory e-mail list)
channels.note: DNREC's map invites subscriptions to the dnrec_beach_monitoring list (by e-mail to the state's listserv) for the beach advisories it issues; the same advisories are on the map and the portal.

channels.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
channels.name: Delaware DNREC (blue-green algae page)
channels.note: Guidance and a reporting route; no dated bloom advisory list was found (2026-11-09). Bloom advisories at monitored beaches appear in the recreational-water history. Watched daily.

channels.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
channels.name: Delaware DNREC (DERNS release notifications)
channels.legal_basis: 7 Del. C. 6014(b): DNREC's central unified notification system notifies, within 12 hours after DNREC is informed of a release, the district's State Representative and Senator, community groups within 5 miles and residents within 5 miles who have registered
channels.note: E-mail, fax or telephone notices of releases to registered recipients; registration needs an account. The public list carries the same releases.

channels.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
channels.name: Delaware DNREC (Environmental Release Notification System, Recent Releases)
channels.legal_basis: 7 Del. C. 6028(a): a person causing an environmental release (sewage of 10,000 gallons or more, 6002(20)) "shall report such an incident to the Department as soon as the person has knowledge"; DNREC posts it on its website "no later than 1 business day after the release is reported"; permitted discharges are exempt
channels.note: DNREC's public list of every environmental release reported under 6028, of every substance, with a detail page each (release and report times, location, facility, Released To, estimated quantity, DNREC's notes). This site keeps the sewage and sanitary-wastewater releases by rule.

channels.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
channels.name: Delaware DNREC (Recreational Water Program advisories)
channels.note: DNREC's advisory and closure history on the state's open-data portal (474 rows since 2001 on 2026-11-14) and the map's 47 sampling stations with their current status; bacteria advisories, not sewage reports.

channels.agency: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
channels.name: Delaware DNREC (shellfish program)
channels.note: Harvest-area classifications and links; emergency closures after a sewage release are announced as state news releases (Indian River Bay, 2026-01-15 and its reopening 2026-02-06). Harvest restrictions, not swimming advisories. Watched daily.

channels.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (ECHO)
channels.note: EPA's eRule sewer overflow and bypass tables: no Delaware row in the current or the all-versions extract on 2026-11-14. Watched daily for Delaware rows.

channels.name: City of Wilmington (alert sign-up)
channels.note: The City's utility pages link an alert sign-up (AlertSense); whether it carries overflow notices was not verified (expansion research, 2026-11-09). Sent to subscribers; no page to read.

channels.name: City of Wilmington (CSO page)
channels.note: The City's explainer of its combined sewers and the outfall signs (the older cso.wilmingtonde.gov site could not be read on 2026-11-09); no overflow status. Watched daily for a notice.

channels.name: City of Wilmington (CSO outfall signs)
channels.legal_basis: EPA's Combined Sewer Overflow Control Policy, minimum control 8 (public notification), carried by NPDES permit DE0020320; the permit's own clause was not read
channels.note: The City says each of its combined sewer outfalls "is marked by a sign notifying the public of the CSO". No overflow notice, status or list was found on the web; Wilmington's overflows are permitted discharges, exempt from DNREC's release list (6028(a)).
